newsitem.title: UK: Dollar draws breath in Europe, halt seen temporary.
newsitem.headline: Dollar draws breath in Europe, halt seen temporary.

text.p: The dollar paused in late Europe after sprinting to a 56-month high against the yen and one-month peak on the mark, with analysts and traders saying the market was recharging itself now for another run.

Although the dollar's rally since late last week had been rapid and was now due for a small correction, economic fundamentals were so much in the dollar's favour that the currency was unlikely to be restrained for long, they said.
"There's been some profit-taking but every time the dollar's pushed lower, there's been solid buying," said Isao Kaneko, senior dealer at Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank in London.

"The trend of selling yen against other currencies is not going to go away so easily. I think the general view is that the dollar will go up for some time, overcoming profit-taking along the way," Kaneko said.

The dollar has risen more than four yen since last Friday, when dollar/yen's latest rally was triggered by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's comment that currencies should not be used as an instrument of trade policy.
The start of Japan's fiscal year on April 1 heralding a fresh flow of investors' funds out of Japan in search of higher yields overseas has added to dollar/yen's strength.
The dollar was at 126.11/16 yen at 1525 GMT after hitting 126.52, its highest level since August 1992, and against 125.76/81 in late European trade on Monday.

It has meanwhile gained five pfennigs against the mark, with a growing perception that European monetary union will go ahead on time putting pressure on the German currency. This followed a meeting of EU finance ministers over the weekend which made progress on details over EMU.
Dollar/mark was at 1.7110/15, off its high of 1.7183 and almost unchanged from late Monday's 1.7106/16.

"The things that helped it (the dollar) on Monday, which is a combination of expectations of higher interest rates and increased optimism about EMU, are factors which suggest we can move up to a test of the 1.7220 (mark) area which was the recent high," said Robert Hayward, economic adviser at BankAmerica.

The immediate concern for the market now was whether and when central banks would intervene to salvage the yen, although traders said they did not expect dollar/yen selling by the authorities at this stage and that verbal intervention so far has been muted.

Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said Japan will deal appropriately with excessive currency moves. Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the finance ministry's international finance bureau, said authorities will be ready to intervene if currency rates veered sharply from fundamentals.
Vice Trade Minister Tsutomu Makino, meanwhile, was quoted by Jiji news agency as saying the weak yen was more positive than negative for the country's economy at the moment.
"At this stage, the Japanese authorities probably feel resigned towards yen weakness to a certain extent," Dai-Ichi Kangyo's Kaneko said.
"It's just that for the sake of the (Tokyo) stock market among other things, the authorities don't want the yen to drop too sharply," Kaneko added.

In any case, dollar/yen selling by the Bank of Japan on its own would have only a temporary impact, and would need cooperation from the U.S. Federal Reserve for a more lasting effect, traders and analysts said.

"There's the perception in the market that Japanese capital would continue to search for higher yields, and given the uncertainty about the single currency project in Europe, it's going into the U.S. markets," BankAmerica's Hayward said.
The yield on Japan's key 10-year government bond hit 2.075 percent on Tuesday, a record low for any benchmark 10-year JGB. In the U.S., the key 10-year Treasury bond yielded 6.89 percent.

Elsewhere in the currency market, the British pound hit a 4-1/2 year high of 2.7915 marks although it later backed off that level to steady around 2.7780, its old floor in the European exchange rate mechanism.
-- Chizu Nomiyama, London Forex Desk, +44-171-542-6721
